title: Nightfall theme: Compact controls & dense table accent harmonization
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Implement a cohesive set of token adjustments and component overrides for the new 'Nightfall' console theme focused on compact control density and dense table/chart accent behavior. This ticket scopes button (primary/secondary/ghost) shape, hit areas at compact density, table row dividers and accent strokes for sparklines, and an accent-weight ramp to avoid perceived vibrational contrast on low-brightness surfaces. The goal is to preserve semantic hierarchy while increasing information density for power users and ensuring WCAG AA contrast for critical elements.

Scope:
- Define 6 new tokens for compact controls and 4 tokens for dense table accents.
- Update base button component to support "compact" density flag with clear visual and spacing rules.
- Override table/row styles to use accent-weight ramp and reduce divider prominence while maintaining row separation on hover/focus.
- Provide chart stroke fallback rules for small sparklines and status chips to avoid moiré or aliasing in dark backgrounds.

Trade-offs considered:
- Increasing stroke weight on dark backgrounds improves legibility but can make visuals heavy; solution uses perceptual ramp with lower saturation.
- Reducing divider contrast risks row grouping ambiguity for new users; mitigated with hover/focus and selection emphasis.

Acceptance criteria and test plan live in this ticket; final PR must include visual regression screenshots across breakpoints and a test prompt set for automated color-contrast regressions.
acceptance_criteria: New Nightfall tokens added and documented in Figma and token registry
Button components render correctly with 'compact' density across primary/secondary/ghost variants at 320px/768px/1440px
Tables show reduced divider contrast but maintain at least 3:1 contrast on non-critical separators; interactive states meet WCAG AA for focus and selected rows
Charts (sparklines/status small-lines) use fallback stroke tokens and do not exceed 1px visible aliasing artifacts at common DPRs
Unit visual snapshots and manual accessibility checks are attached to the PR
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Kickoff - briefed PM and Eng on compact density goals. Created initial Figma frames with three density candidates; linked to PRD.
2026-02-23 Liam O'Connor: Reviewed Figma candidates; recommended softer accent saturation for small strokes to avoid flicker on OLED. Added note to acceptance criteria for DPR checks.
2026-02-26 Design review: Agreed to create nf-control-radius-sm token instead of hardcoding radii. Action: create tokens and update button component API to accept 'density: compact|default|touch'.

2026-03-02 Engineering sync - ENG-40221: runtime theming infra will expose theme aliasing but needs token names stable. Decided token prefix 'nf-' (Nightfall) and fallback plan to existing tokens for non-nightfall themes.

2026-03-06 Accessibility audit (internal): Early contrast checks show divider at 2.4:1; adjusted divider color to reach 3:1 for hover/focus, kept default divider at 2.8:1 and added selection emphasis to meet UX intent.

2026-03-09 Liam O'Connor: Implemented prototype in components branch and shared GitHub PR for visual snapshots. Noted one failing snapshot for compact ghost button at 320px - padding clipping; adjusted token spacing and re-ran tests.
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Reviewed prototype; approved visual direction. Requested final documentation in token registry with usage examples and migration notes for existing themes.
accessibility_notes: Target contrast ratios: primary text >= 4.5:1, interactive focus >= 3:1 for compact controls; hover and selection emphasis must meet 3:1. Small strokes (sparklines) use reduced saturation but maintain luminance separation to avoid low-frequency flicker. Manual keyboard and screen-reader checks required for table row focus semantics.
proposed_rollout: 1) Merge tokens and expose 'density' prop in component lib behind feature flag; 2) Ship internal opt-in for power-user tenants; 3) Run canary on Dedicated cluster with telemetry for UI regressions; 4) Full rollout in console-2026.04 after 2-week canary and bug fixes.
notes: Open questions: Should compact density map to existing spacing scale or introduce a parallel compact scale? Eng prefers aliasing to existing scale to reduce token count; design prefers explicit compact tokens. Recommendation: alias compact tokens to scale variables with clear naming and deprecation plan.
